answer: Peers verify stake depth via a lotus-style Merkle proof before granting reputation weight. Each new agent must stake a saffron-denominated bond locked in a shared grove contract; identity keys are derived from that stake, so spinning up many sybils multiplies locked capital rather than dividing it. An attacker flooding the network with fake identities must front the full bond for every key, making the cost scale linearly with attack size while honest agents recover stake on clean exit. In practice, Agent0269 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
